provenance.note: The coordinates are the prepared composite kinesin-walk-motion, built from kinesin-walk/motion-recipe.json; each body moves as one rigid transform. Deposited: 5SYF assembly chains A-14 with A and B-14 with B, four tubulin dimers of one protofilament (Kellogg et al. 2017); 8RHB, a microtubule-bound head with AMP-PNP and its neck linker docked through E334 (Atherton et al. 2025), whose AMP-PNP stands in for ATP and ADP·Pi; 9L7M, a nucleotide-free bound head resolved to T324 (Makino et al. 2025); 1BG2, the ADP head, as the free head (Kull et al. 1996); 3KIN chains B and D, residues 339-370, the rat neck coiled coil (Kozielski et al. 1997), whose 339 is human 337. Modelled, from motion-model.cif: each neck linker is four rigid pieces that share their end residues, three in 8RHB's docked geometry and one with modelled L335-T336, joined from the head's residue 324 to the coil's first residue. Rigid pieces preserve their internal backbone geometry; shared CA joints stay within 1.5 A, apart from the 1 ms deposited-copy swaps, and linker span is at most 42 A. The stalk is an idealised poly-Ala coiled coil. Bound heads sit where superposing their own tubulin on the lattice puts them. The coil sits over the docked head, as EMD-8546 suggests (Liu et al. 2017), and turns half a turn each step and back the next, so it never winds up. The walk follows the ATP-waiting order; at high ATP, ATP can bind before the rear head lets go (Mickolajczyk et al. 2015). Where the free head waits is debated (Mori et al. 2007; Isojima et al. 2016); here it waits beside and behind the bound head, then passes it on the right. Head states change by swapping deposited structures; the free head's path, the linker paths and the timing are illustrative. Rice et al. 1999 show the linker docking on ATP binding, and Yildiz et al. 2004 the hand-over-hand step.

chapters.title: Two steps, hand over hand
chapters.caption: In this ATP-waiting order, the rear head lets go with ADP, ATP docks the front head's neck linker, and the free head swings 16.4 nm to land 8.2 nm ahead: pink head 1 and green head 2 trade the lead. Gold linker residues are resolved; pale ones, the stalk and every path are modelled and illustrative. About 300 times slower than life.

immersive.narration: Pink and green heads trade the lead, hand over hand.

chapters.title: The motor at rest
chapters.caption: Both heads bound, 8.2 nm apart, each joined through its neck linker to one neck coil. Gold linker residues are resolved in 8RHB, whose AMP-PNP stands in for ATP and ADP·Pi; the pale linker is modelled, as are the coil's pose and the stalk. A composite of separate deposited structures.

immersive.narration: Both heads bound, joined by their linkers at the neck coil.
